subject: Cognitive Science
title: Sensory Substitution
description: A micro-lesson that makes Sensory Substitution usable.

hook.text: A blind man wears a camera on his head that converts images to vibrations on his tongue. After training, he 'sees.'

buildup.text: Paul Bach-y-Rita pioneered sensory substitution: delivering visual information through touch or sound.

discovery.text: After weeks of training, the visual cortex of blind users activates—proving the brain reassigns its resources.

twist.text: These users don't report 'feeling vibrations.' They report spatial experiences—something genuinely visual-like.

climax.text: Sensory substitution suggests the brain doesn't care which sense delivers data—it cares about the information's structure.

punchline.text: The brain doesn't see with eyes—it sees with data.

quiz.question: What happens in blind users' brains during sensory substitution?
